this paper introduces a very novel and interesting approach to the reinforcement learning problem with sparse feedback, which has been shown to be very successful in practice and theoretically justified by a regret bound.
RESLOPE is a novel reinforcement learning algorithm that solves the credit assignment problem for sparse reward environments by automatically learning a loss representation.
RESLOPE can be applied to a wide range of tasks and it is able to achieve a competitive performance with the state-of-the-art algorithms.

The main takeaway from our work is that
, even when only the final episode loss is available, it is still possible to learn a representation of a dense loss function that allows to solve the problem with no regret.
, even in the absence of incremental feedback, it may still be possible to learn an internal representation that allows for a more effective exploration-exploitation trade-off.
, in the absence of incremental loss feedback, the problem of reinforcement learning can be reduced to a contextual bandit problem.
